 package slugify
 
+import (
+	"errors"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+const maxSlugLength = 48
+
+// Slugify normalizes value into a lowercase, hyphen-separated slug composed
+// only of ASCII letters and digits. Runs of any other character are
+// collapsed into a single hyphen, and leading/trailing hyphens are trimmed.
+// The result is capped at 48 bytes, trimming a trailing hyphen left by
+// truncation. If the normalized value contains no letters or digits, an
+// error is returned.
 func Slugify(value string) (string, error) {
-	return value, nil
+	var b strings.Builder
+	lastHyphen := false
+
+	for _, r := range value {
+		switch {
+		case r >= 'a' && r <= 'z', r >= '0' && r <= '9':
+			b.WriteRune(r)
+			lastHyphen = false
+		case r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z':
+			b.WriteRune(r + ('a' - 'A'))
+			lastHyphen = false
+		default:
+			if !lastHyphen {
+				b.WriteByte('-')
+				lastHyphen = true
+			}
+		}
+	}
+
+	slug := strings.Trim(b.String(), "-")
+	if slug == "" {
+		return "", errors.New("slugify: value contains no letters or digits")
+	}
+
+	if len(slug) > maxSlugLength {
+		slug = strings.TrimRight(slug[:maxSlugLength], "-")
+	}
+
+	return slug, nil
 }
